words.prose: {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) does not open an ordinary address, because no named addressee follows it. Before {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}), it turns the wish into a cried-out lament: the grammar has the shape of calling, but the force is exclamatory anguish. The compact opening {{ar:يَا لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:yā laytahā}}) front-loads regret before the predicate explains what is being wished, and it answers the earlier condemned cry {{ar:يَا لَيْتَنِي}} ({{tr:yā laytanī}}) (69:25) with a second lament unit. Its long opening sound also helps the short ayah begin as a drawn-out cry before the tighter closing phrase.

topics.headline: vocative form becomes lament
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening sounds like a call but does not summon anyone; the address particle has been converted into lament-force.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) as a vocative particle used formulaically before {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}), with no overt vocative complement.

topics.headline: particle stacking intensifies the wish
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the wish is not neutral statement of desire; the extra exclamatory layer raises it into desperation.
topics.reason: The local construction begins with a vocative particle immediately before the optative particle, and the guardrail evidence licenses the whole opening as an optative nominal construction.

topics.headline: one compact opening cry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening as one compressed lament unit, not as a detached particle followed by a separate wish.
topics.reason: The surface and translation-support evidence both treat {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) with {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}) as a compressed exclamatory opening.

topics.headline: regret arrives before explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah begin with regret itself before the clause specifies the wished final state.
topics.reason: The attachment clauses confirm that the exclamatory-optative opening precedes the predicate content {{ar:كَانَتِ ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:kānati l-qāḍiyata}}).

topics.headline: second condemned lament unit

topics.reason: The CRITICAL row gives the repeated lament construction, and the local guardrail evidence confirms that this opening functions as an exclamatory wish.

words.prose: {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}) is more than a wish word: {{ar:لَيْتَ}} ({{tr:layta}}) governs the attached {{ar:هَا}} ({{tr:hā}}) as its subject slot, so the wish arrives already carrying an unresolved feminine matter. The pronoun is definite enough to point back into the discourse, but the ayah does not name it; that lets death, the account, and the whole predicament remain gathered under one suffix. The construction turns the confession of not knowing in 69:26 into impossible desire, and because the ayah ends without a balancing correction, the wish is left hanging against the final predicate. The {{ar:لَيْتُهَا}} ({{tr:laytuhā}}) vowel variant is useful as attachment evidence, while the local function remains the same optative frame.

topics.headline: wish particle governs the suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the suffix is not decorative; it is the governed subject around which the rest of the wished clause is built.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the suffix in {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}) as the governed noun of {{ar:لَيْتَ}} ({{tr:layta}}), and the following predicate content belongs to that wish.

topics.headline: definite pronoun keeps the referent open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one small feminine suffix gather death, reckoning, and the speaker's situation without forcing a single named antecedent.
topics.reason: The cross-reference and translation-support evidence explicitly preserve ambiguity for the feminine suffix, while the verb agreement remains syntactically controlled by it.

topics.headline: one suffix routes several wishes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the wish as asking that death, the reckoning, or the whole predicament had become the decisive end.
topics.reason: The guardrail evidence does not resolve the suffix to one overt antecedent, and the predicate {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}) supplies the terminal characterization that makes the multi-route wish coherent.

topics.headline: knowing collapses into impossible wish
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the discourse move from failed knowledge to a counterfactual wish that cannot be answered inside the ayah.
topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}) as optative, and the local clause ends with the wished predicate rather than a corrective response.

topics.headline: wish and object arrive together

topics.reason: The local surface combines the optative particle with its suffix, and attachment evidence makes that suffix the governed complement of the particle.

topics.reason: The variant affects the vowel on the particle-pronoun complex, but the local guardrails still identify the word as the optative particle with attached {{ar:هَا}} ({{tr:hā}}).

words.prose: {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}}) supplies the missed pastness of the wish: the speaker wants the matter to have already been the end, while the grammar shows that this state was not realized. It is {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) as a defective copular verb, not an existential main verb; it bridges the governed suffix of {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}) to {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}). Its feminine singular form keeps the hidden antecedent, the verb, and the predicate in one agreement chain. The being-root is therefore turned toward wished non-continuation: existence-language carries a desire for settled ending. The larger {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) field, including creative-command contexts such as 2:117, is only a contrast here; this is no effective command, but a powerless counterfactual. Within the surah, the same being-language also links this impossible wish to the later characterization at 69:33. The kasra before {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}) also pulls the verb into the predicate as one connected closing phrase.

topics.headline: perfect verb makes the wish unrealized past
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wish asks for finality to have already been true, which the lament itself admits did not happen.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as perfect 3fs, and the attachment evidence places it inside the {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}) wish clause.

topics.headline: copular bridge into finality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the verb does not simply say something existed; it turns the unresolved pronoun into a predicate characterization of finality.
topics.reason: Attachment marks {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}) as the predicate of {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}}), and the verb-instance frame is copular with no object.

topics.headline: 3fs agreement holds the hidden referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the masculine speaker is not the grammatical center; the clause is organized around the unnamed feminine matter.
topics.reason: QAC gives {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}}) as 3fs, and attachment evidence states that its implicit subject agreement is controlled by the feminine pronoun in {{ar:لَيْتَهَا}} ({{tr:laytahā}}).

topics.headline: being-language carries wished ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the irony that a root of being supplies the grammar for wanting existence to have reached finality.
topics.reason: The positive contrast survives, but V4 and local grammar narrow {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) here to temporal/copular predication rather than activating all being-derived branches.

topics.headline: creative command field is inverted as contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader contrasts powerful being-command language with this powerless counterfactual wish for termination.
topics.reason: The k-w-n/q-d-y decree field, including 2:117, is meaningful as contrast, but the local verb remains perfect {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}}) in an optative clause, not a creative imperative.

topics.headline: same-surah being-language echo

topics.reason: The CRITICAL row gives the same-surah echo at 69:33, and no local evidence contradicts retaining it as a discourse thread.

topics.headline: kasra connects verb to predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verb and final predicate move as one connected phrase rather than as a restarted ending.
topics.reason: QAC notes the kasra on the feminine tāʾ for liaison before hamzat al-waṣl, and attachment evidence joins the verb directly to its predicate.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}) closes the ayah as a definite predicate: not any possible ending, but the recognizable decisive finality the speaker wishes had settled everything. As the accusative predicate of {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}}), it classifies the unresolved pronoun rather than narrating a new event; the wish is that the matter had been finality itself. The {{ar:ق ض ي}} ({{tr:q-ḍ-y}}) field lets verdict, completion, fulfilled obligation, and settled account reinforce each other, so in the reckoning context the word is more than biological death: it is the account closed with no further claim. Its active participle form casts finality as the deciding or finishing one, while its rare definite feminine participial shape concentrates the root's broad decree-language into one marked title for the end. The root's eschatological decision field is visible beside {{ar:قُضِيَ ٱلْأَمْرُ}} ({{tr:quḍiya l-amru}}) (19:39), though here it is turned into the condemned speaker's wish. The qiraat contrast {{ar:ٱلْقَاصِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāṣiyata}}) narrows to apparatus value: it shows how a dot-shift would move the mechanism from termination to remoteness, while the local canonical word keeps decisive completion at the center. That root-shift also makes the heavy middle consonant semantically load-bearing rather than ornamental sound.

topics.headline: the known decisive end
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker is not asking for some vague ending, but for the known final closure that would have sealed the account.
topics.reason: QAC and noun-instance evidence identify the word as definite, feminine, and accusative, and the local ayah closes on it without a following qualification.

topics.headline: predicate quality, not separate event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that death or reckoning is being characterized as finality, not that a new action is being narrated after the wish.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}) as the accusative predicate of {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}}), and translation support warns against treating it as a separate object.

topics.headline: feminine accusative completes the chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the final word fit the hidden feminine referent through agreement and predicate case.
topics.reason: The word is feminine singular accusative, matching the suffix-governed clause and functioning as {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}})'s predicate.

topics.headline: verdict and account-closure finality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the end as judicial verdict, completed settlement, and ledger closure at once, because the previous reckoning scene presses those branches together.
topics.reason: V4 accepts q-d-y branches for decisive judgment, completion, death as enacted end, and settling dues; local grammar narrows them into the predicate of final settlement rather than activating unrelated branches.

topics.headline: death wished as absolute terminality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wish is not simply for death, but for death to have had the property of ending the reopened account.
topics.reason: The unresolved pronoun can include death or reckoning, and the q-d-y predicate supplies decisive finality in the context of the previous account question.

topics.headline: finality as an acting finisher
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees finality cast in an agent-like form, as the deciding or finishing one rather than a flat abstract noun.
topics.reason: QAC marks the local word as a feminine active participle functioning substantively as the predicate.

topics.headline: rare participial title for the end
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a broad and common root is concentrated into a sparse, marked participial form at the ayah's final word.
topics.reason: The contextual profiles mark the q-d-y active participle as low-occurrence, and the local noun-instance evidence gives the exact definite feminine accusative predicate shape.

topics.headline: decree-language becomes a wished end
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the q-d-y field of decisive decree behind the word, while recognizing that this occurrence is the condemned speaker's wished closure.
topics.reason: V4 supports decisive ruling and completion branches, and the CRITICAL row gives the eschatological parallel at 19:39; local syntax narrows the echo to a predicate in a wish clause.

topics.headline: being-root tied to finality-root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the clause fuse being-language with decisive completion, making existence itself the thing wished closed.
topics.reason: The contextual collocation profile links the local q-d-y active participle with k-w-n, and attachment evidence binds {{ar:كَانَتِ}} ({{tr:kānati}}) directly to {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}).

topics.headline: dot-shift variant changes the mechanism
topics.reader_payoff: The reader gains a variant-reading contrast between wished termination and wished remoteness, without replacing the canonical final-settlement reading.
topics.reason: The qiraat contrast changes the consonantal root from q-d-y to q-ṣ-y, so it is valuable as apparatus contrast, while the aligned local surface remains {{ar:ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ}} ({{tr:al-qāḍiyata}}) from {{ar:ق ض ي}} ({{tr:q-ḍ-y}}).

topics.headline: emphatic consonant carries lexical weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the heavy consonant belongs to the root contrast itself, so the sound and the lexical mechanism reinforce each other.
topics.reason: The sound observation is kept only as tied to the {{ar:ض}} ({{tr:ḍ}}) versus {{ar:ص}} ({{tr:ṣ}}) root contrast, not as independent phonetic symbolism.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The counterfactual construction ياليتها كانت القاضية anchors finality in كانت and the feminine predicate القاضية.
baseline_models.mechanism: Temporal occurrence is wished to have coincided with an enacted death and complete expiration, so an earlier event would have left no remainder capable of entering the speaker's present.

activation_trace.role: Being or occurrence in time makes the wish counterfactually recast what an earlier event was.
Death as an enacted end supplies the wished-for terminal event.
Completion and expiration sharpen death into an end that exhausts every sequel.

changed_reading.before: A bare lament that something had happened differently.
changed_reading.after: A wish that the earlier event had been an actually enacted, remainderless death or expiration.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The definite predicate القاضية can characterize the wished antecedent as the event that decisively settles a matter.
baseline_models.mechanism: The wish retrospectively assigns an earlier occurrence the force of a binding ruling, not merely the property of being over.

activation_trace.role: Temporal predication provides the counterfactual reassignment of the antecedent's status.
A decisive ruling or binding settlement makes القاضية the event that would close a case.

changed_reading.before: The speaker simply wishes for an end.
changed_reading.after: The speaker wishes that an earlier occurrence had itself possessed final adjudicative force.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The due-settlement branch of ق ض ي remains attached to القاضية, while كانت asks that this settlement already have occurred.
baseline_models.mechanism: Finality is modeled as a liability fully paid or collected: the wished event would not only stop life but discharge whatever remained outstanding.

activation_trace.role: Past occurrence locates the wished discharge before the present lament.
Settling or collecting a due supplies a transactional image of exhaustive closure.

changed_reading.after: Finality also means that no claim, debt, or obligation survives the wished event.

context_deltas.mechanism: A delivered written record is publicly read and exposes a reckoning. That sequence turns the focus's decisive-settlement branch into a procedural counterfactual: the speaker wishes the disclosed record had closed the case instead of initiating what follows.

activation_trace.role: The decisive ruling anchors the changed reading in القاضية as case-closing force.
A written inscription that imposes judgment gives the prospective ruling a documentary substrate.
Reading and recitation move the record from possession into public disclosure.
Counting and account identify the matter that the wished decisive event would have settled.

structural_cues: The two recipients are introduced through mirrored book-delivery and speech scenes.
The focus follows the second recipient's refusal of both book and knowledge of the account.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delivery, inscription, reading, account, and decisive ruling; I supply the procedural arrow from disclosure to hoped-for case closure. A live alternative is that القاضية names death alone and the legal sequence merely explains the lament.

changed_reading.before: القاضية is an unspecified decisive event.
changed_reading.after: القاضية is the wished final disposition of a documentary reckoning that has instead opened into enforcement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The successful sequence realizes a satisfying life, elevated garden, near fruit, and days made past through a cadence of feminine predicates. القاضية enters the same cadence as a negative counter-state: the failed recipient can name no inhabitable good condition and instead wishes for the condition that cancels all further conditions.

activation_trace.role: Completion and expiration make the focus predicate an anti-state that ends the descriptive series.
Death as enacted end gives that anti-state its terminal force.
Satisfaction opposed to displeasure supplies the achieved affective state against which القاضية turns.
The non-dominant mapped branch preserves acceptance as a second convergent scope of the positive predicate.
Elevation gives the positive state a realized vertical dimension.
Nearness makes the positive provision accessible rather than merely promised.
Time that has passed completes the positive sequence's temporal dimension.

structural_cues: راضية, عالية, دانية, خالية, and القاضية form a conspicuous feminine cadence across the two outcomes.
The earlier predicates describe possessed states, whereas القاضية occurs only inside an unrealized wish.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the recurring feminine forms and their affective, spatial, and temporal branches; I infer that their ordered cadence makes القاضية a counter-state rather than an isolated rhyme. The live alternative is phonological parallelism without a shared semantic mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The focus is an isolated wish for death.
changed_reading.after: The wish answers the other recipient's achieved states with a single unrealized anti-state: let there have been no state after the finalizer.

context_deltas.mechanism: What was advanced in prior days becomes an account; the successful side receives untroubled provision, while the failed side is identified by not mobilizing provision for the immobilized poor and receives a harsh anti-food. The due-settlement branch of القاضية therefore becomes a wish that death could have discharged an obligation which the context presents as still collectible.

activation_trace.role: Settling and collecting dues anchors the focus in an outstanding-obligation model.
The account supplies the explicit ledger whose balance remains unknown to the speaker.
Property advanced beforehand gives prior conduct the structure of value paid forward.
Feeding another supplies the omitted social due rather than food as private consumption alone.
Sustenance that stabilizes residence makes feeding materially restore a person whose condition has arrested movement.
The branch's heat and severity turn the received food into punitive provision rather than discharge.

structural_cues: The feast for what was advanced precedes the focus, while failure to urge feeding and the exclusive punitive food follow it.
The causal explanation in 69:33-34 interrupts the enforcement sequence to identify what remained morally unpaid.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies advance, account, omitted feeding, stabilizing sustenance, and punitive food; I supply the reciprocal arrow that treats omission as an unpaid due collected after the wish. The live alternative is a moral contrast without transactional equivalence.

changed_reading.before: The wished end would settle an unspecified liability.
changed_reading.after: The speaker wishes death could discharge the account, but the food reversal exposes a social due that survives and returns as collection.

context_deltas.mechanism: Past days, the severe present day, and the later causal كان make time porous: prior conduct remains present as evidence. The focus's كانت القاضية is consequently a wish for a temporal seal that would make the past truly expire, while the repeated كان demonstrates that the speaker's former mode of being has crossed into today.

activation_trace.role: Temporal predication anchors the wish to what the antecedent should already have become.
Expiration supplies the desired impermeable boundary after the earlier event.
The present day's event and severity provide the temporal destination the past has entered.
The passing away of time marks prior days as gone without making their effects empty.
The repeated past predication carries former nonbelief forward as the cause of present enforcement.

structural_cues: 69:24 labels the earlier days past, 69:27 wishes for expiration, and 69:35 insists on today.
The second كان in 69:33 introduces enduring causal biography after the wished temporal closure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies past days, today, repeated كان, and expiration; I infer that remembered conduct crosses the boundary the speaker wants sealed. A live alternative is ordinary retrospection with no special temporal mechanism in the focus.

changed_reading.before: كانت simply places a desired ending in the past.
changed_reading.after: كانت asks for a past made causally dead, but the later كان shows that the speaker's past remains operative in the present.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the wish, wealth loses sufficiency and authority receives the verb of perishing, yet the speaker remains available to be seized. The sequence clarifies القاضية as desired terminality for the self, sharply distinguished from the mere collapse of the self's supports and proxies.

activation_trace.role: Death as enacted end locates the requested extinction in the speaker rather than in possessions.
Exhaustive expiration distinguishes terminality from partial dispossession.
Failed sufficiency shows that an external resource cannot answer the present need.
Accumulated wealth supplies the first proxy that falls away without ending its owner.
Perishing is grammatically assigned to authority, making the speaker's own non-perishing conspicuous.
Power and jurisdiction identify the protective proxy that perishes before arrest.

structural_cues: The first two clauses after 69:27 strip away wealth and authority before commands act directly on the person.
Only the speaker's authority is said to perish; the speaker persists as the object of four ensuing commands.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed wealth, perished authority, and the still-seizable person; I infer a deliberate proxy-versus-self contrast that specifies what القاضية was wanted to terminate. The live alternative is that هلك سلطانيه is only a conventional statement of lost power.

changed_reading.before: The lament asks generally for death to have been final.
changed_reading.after: The lament asks for the self, not merely its wealth or authority, to have received the perishing that the next verses pointedly withhold from it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The post-focus commands carry out arrest, restraint, exposure to fire, and insertion into a chain. They activate ق ض ي as execution of an action while frustrating its death-and-expiration branches: everything is executed except the terminal end the speaker requested.

activation_trace.role: Perfected execution gives the following commands the form of an action carried fully through.
Death as enacted end supplies the result that the command sequence never grants.
Capture and arrest initiate execution against a subject who remains present.
A collar that binds the body converts judgment into durable restraint.
Meeting the fire supplies bodily enforcement without semantic completion.
The non-dominant mapped root independently preserves contact with fire as the operative image.
Insertion of one thing into another makes the final command continue the process rather than end it.

structural_cues: Four imperatives advance stepwise from seizure to chaining, fire, and insertion.
The focus requests one finalizer, but the response is a serial procedure with repeated ثم and فاء transitions.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a perfected-action branch and an ordered enforcement sequence; I infer that the sequence enacts one sense of قضاء while denying its death sense. A live alternative is that the commands merely narrate punishment after an independently understood death wish.

changed_reading.before: القاضية fuses execution and terminal result into one wished event.
changed_reading.after: The context splits them: judgment is relentlessly executed, but execution does not become the terminal death the speaker wanted.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it maps the joining branch of writing onto literal bodily linkage. It remains anchored in القاضية as decisive ruling and in the packet's record-to-chain order, but downstream prose should present it as a cross-domain material analogy, not as the lexical meaning of كتاب or القاضية.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: القاضية anchors a decisive verdict whose binding force can be tracked from written record to attached body.

activation_trace.role: A binding ruling supplies the legal force that the material sequence makes physical.
Joining one thing to another exposes a latent material image inside the delivered record.
The collar turns abstract binding into restraint at the body.
Connected rings extend binding into a serial material structure.
Insertion completes the analogy by placing the judged person inside the linked structure.

changed_reading.before: The book contains a judgment and the chain later enforces it.
changed_reading.after: The wished decisive closure fails because documentary binding propagates into bodily binding, link after link.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because ordinary كانت is temporal predication, not an overt suretyship form. It remains worth carrying because the focus inventory explicitly supplies the undertaking branch and the context removes wealth, authority, and intimate support in sequence; prose must label it a latent root resonance rather than a grammatical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The suretyship branch remains tied to the focus root ك و ن in كانت, while القاضية supplies the ruling against which surety would matter.

activation_trace.role: Undertaking responsibility activates the odd possibility that the wished antecedent should have stood for the speaker.
The binding ruling establishes the pressure under which a guarantor would be sought.
Failed sufficiency removes wealth as something able to answer for the speaker.
Lost power and jurisdiction remove institutional protection.
The absent close relation removes personal kinship support as the last possible surety.

changed_reading.before: كانت only asks what the antecedent had been.
changed_reading.after: At the edge of the root inventory, the lament also sounds like a wish that something had undertaken the speaker's case when every worldly sponsor failed.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the waterskin-decay branch of ق ض ي against the usual death and completion senses. It remains anchored in القاضية and gains a mechanism from explicit failure to urge feeding plus the later wash-derived punitive substance; prose should frame it as an analogy of cumulative neglect, never as a direct translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The rare neglect-decay branch is cited directly from القاضية and changes the temporal texture of its finality.

activation_trace.role: A waterskin spoiled by being left too long supplies finality as accumulated deterioration rather than one sudden stroke.
Urging toward action, explicitly negated in context, makes omission causally visible.
Feeding another identifies the unattended material responsibility.
The washing medium and what is washed in it retain the container-and-residue material field of spoilage.

changed_reading.before: القاضية imagines a sudden final stroke.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it can also expose an end produced by long moral neglect, with the unattended obligation returning as spoiled provision.

strongest_changes: The book, public reading, and account turn a generic decisive end into the wished final disposition of a documentary proceeding.
The feminine cadence makes القاضية an unrealized anti-state set against the other recipient's satisfying, elevated, near, and completed states.
Failed wealth and perished authority distinguish loss of proxies from terminality of the self.
The arrest-to-chain sequence executes judgment perfectly while denying the completion or death requested by القاضية.
The feast, omitted feeding, and punitive food strengthen the exploratory reading of finality as discharge of an unpaid social due.
summary.what_was_special: Only two focus roots generate several live mechanisms: temporal seal, enacted death, decisive verdict, completed execution, and settled due. Context does not collapse them; it repeatedly separates procedural execution from terminal result and lets legal, temporal, material, social, and morphological readings coexist.
remaining_uncertainties: The feminine pronoun's antecedent is not resolved by the focus line itself, so documentary, experiential, and death-oriented attachments must remain distinct.
The procedural and debt models may be contextual overlays on the terminal-death reading rather than independent lexical construals.
The suretyship and neglect-decay outliers are intentionally branch-distant and should remain qualified latent resonances.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A wish for death as completed ending.** **ق ض ي B003** (death as an enacted end) is selected by `القاضية`, while 69:30-32 shows continued punitive sequence. The packet supplies the wish and the nonfinal continuation; I infer that the speaker desires the earlier death to have exhausted all consequence. The ayah reads as longing for termination, not merely another verdict.
2. **Finality desired against an unfinished account.** **ق ض ي B004** (completion and coming to an end) remains active beside B003. The packet supplies a completed earthly span but an ongoing post-account process; I infer that what is wished for is absolute closure. This reading retains death and completion without forcing one to displace the other.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 69:30-32 supplies the correction: death was not the terminating completion wished for, because custody and insertion continue.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Death is desired as an enacted endpoint.** `ق ض ي` B003 is "death as an enacted end" and B004 is "completion and expiration." The speaker has received the adverse record, and the next ayat remove wealth and authority before commands carry him through shackling, fire, and chain. B003 assigns `ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ` the role of the earlier death; B004 specifies the wished-for property that it did not have: final completion. The packet supplies the wish and continued sequence; I infer that ongoing liability makes non-final death newly intolerable. The line reads as a wish that death had exhausted the process rather than opened another stage.
2. **The wished-for ending is also a decisive ruling.** `ق ض ي` B001 is "decisive ruling or command." The noun is followed by a cascade of imperatives in 69:30-32, showing that a different judgment is in fact being executed. B001 makes the speaker's wish juridical: he wants the prior death to have disposed of the case. The packet supplies wish then commands; I infer that execution of the actual ruling reveals the unavailable alternative. `ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ` can therefore mean not just annihilating death but the decision that would have closed jurisdiction.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 69:46 later supplies an actual life-ending mechanism in the hypothetical cutting of `ٱلْوَتِينَ`. That scene concretizes `ق ض ي` B003/B004: an enacted end requires severing the conduit of persistence, whereas the speaker's prior death evidently did not complete liability. The comparison narrows the wish to procedural finality, not a generalized desire for any destruction.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ölümün bir kişiye erişip yaşamını sona erdirmesini, kişinin ölmesini, birini öldürmeyi ve ölümü kaçınılmaz biçimde uygulanan son olarak adlandırmayı birlikte destekler. Geçici çerçevedeki ölüm ve öldürücü sonuç sınırı bu kanıtla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca yaşamın sona ermesi veya sona erdirilmesiyle ilgilidir; genel bitirme ve tamamlanma anlamları bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, ölümle ilgili ad biçimlerini ve yalnızca verilen söz öbeklerinde ortaya çıkan ölme ya da öldürme anlamlarını ayrı tutar; bunlar çıplak biçime tek bir genel anlam olarak yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Ölümün bir canlıya erişerek yaşamı kesin biçimde sona erdirmesi veya bir eylemin o canlının ölümüne yol açmasıdır.

facets.statement: Ölümün gerçekleşmesiyle bir canlının yaşamının kesin olarak sona ermesi.
Bir eylemle canlının yaşamını sona erdirip onu öldürme.
Ölümü, kaçınılmaz biçimde yürürlüğe giren son veya öldürücü güç olarak adlandırma.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, ölümün gerçekleşmesi ile birini öldürme kullanımlarını ortaklaşa verir ve ölümün geri çevrilemeyen, uygulanan bir son olarak adlandırılmasını bu çekirdeğe bağlar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın yaşamı sona erdiren temel olayını hem kendiliğinden gerçekleşen ölüm hem de öldürme yönleriyle karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Yaşamın kesin sona erişini ve bu sonun bir eylemle gerçekleştirilebilmesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Ölümün kişiye eriştiği ve yaşamın sona erdiği söz öbeklerinde doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Canlının yaşamının ölümle sona ermesi yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir başkasının eylemiyle öldürme ve ölümü adlandırma yönlerini dışarıda bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir gereksinimi, ibadeti, süreyi veya başka bir işi tamamlayıp bitirme ile bir şeyin geçip gitmesi, tükenmesi ve yok olması aşamalarını açıkça destekler. Geçici çerçeve, tamamlanan eylem ile sona eren şey arasındaki katılımcı farkını koruduğu sürece uygundur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal hem bir işi bitirmeyi hem de bir şeyin sona erip tükenmesini kapsar; ölüm ve borç ödeme ancak kendi ayrı dallarında ele alınır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, sona erme bildiren biçim ile belirli iş, gereksinim, ibadet ve süre söz öbeklerini ayırır; bu kalıpların bütün ayrıntıları çıplak biçime yüklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir işi, gereksinimi, ibadeti veya süreyi son sınırına ulaştırıp tamamlamak; ya da bir şeyin süresi dolarak geçip gitmesi, tükenmesi ve ortadan kalkmasıdır.

facets.statement: Bir işi veya süreci gereken son sınıra ulaştırarak tamamlayıp bitirme.
Bir şeyin süresi veya varlığı sona ererek geçip gitmesi ve tükenmesi.
Bir işin artık geri alınamayacak biçimde kesin olarak sonuçlanması.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, bir işi bitirip ondan çıkma ile bir şeyin süresinin veya varlığının tükenip gitmesini aynı sona ulaşma çevresinde birleştirir; bazı kullanımlarda sonuç geri alınamaz duruma gelir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi yapmak, biçimlendirmek ve kusursuzca tamamlamak ile tasarlanan eylemi kararlılıkla yürürlüğe koymayı ortak bir sonuçlandırma çekirdeğinde destekler. Geçici çerçevedeki yaratma ve yapma örnekleri, genel bir var etme anlamına genişletilmeden bu sınır içinde kullanılabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca yapma, kusursuzca tamamlama ve eylemi yürürlüğe koyma çekirdeğidir; salt planlama, ölçme veya sözlü karar verme değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, yapıp kusursuzca tamamlama çekirdeğini belirli yaratma, iş görme ve sağlam ürün söz öbeklerinden ayırır; bu örneklerin özel kapsamı çıplak biçime taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi yapıp biçim vererek sağlam ve kusursuz duruma getirmek veya tasarlanan bir eylemi kararlılıkla gerçekleştirip yürürlüğe koymaktır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi yapma, biçimlendirme ve işi kusursuzca tamamlayarak sağlam duruma getirme.
Tasarlanan eylemi kararlılıkla gerçekleştirip amaçlanan sonuca kadar yürütme.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, bir şeyi yapıp kusursuzca tamamlamayı ve istenen eylemi sonuca kadar yürütmeyi ortaklaştırır; yaratma örneği de ortaya çıkarma ile işi bitirme aşamalarını birlikte taşır.
